policies.state_body: Office of Renewable Energy Siting and Electric Transmission (ORES), Department of Public Service
policies.summary: For facilities under ORES review, ORES may decline to apply a local law found unreasonably burdensome in view of the state's climate targets, and once a municipality has notice of the application it may not require its own approval, permit or other condition except as Article VIII allows.

When the New York Power Authority, its subsidiaries, its public-private partners or anyone acting for it develop renewable projects under Public Authorities Law 1005(27-a) or (27-b), they may not build on land used in agricultural production (except generator lead lines and interconnection equipment, or an agrivoltaics project), and may not build on Native American territory or reservations without the nation's consent and any required federal consent.

policies.state_body: Office of Renewable Energy Siting and Electric Transmission (ORES), Department of Public Service
policies.summary: Renewable energy facilities of 25 MW or more, with any co-located storage, need an ORES siting permit under Public Service Law Article VIII; smaller facilities get no state siting permit and stay under municipal land use control. Battery storage that is not co-located with such a facility is outside the ORES rules.
policies.statute_citation: N.Y. Pub. Serv. Law sections 137(4), 140(1) (Article VIII); 16 NYCRR 1100-1.1(d)(5), 1100-1.2(bb)

policies.state_body: Office of Renewable Energy Siting and Electric Transmission (ORES), Department of Public Service
policies.summary: ORES rules set uniform setbacks for facilities it permits: wind turbines 2 times total height from non-participating residences and 1.1 times from property lines and public roads; solar 250 feet from non-participating occupied residences and 100 feet from non-participating residential property lines, with arrays no taller than 20 feet. Noise outside non-participating homes is capped at 45 dBA Leq (2-hour) for wind and 45 dBA Leq (1-hour) for solar.

Legal basis: Town of Boston Local Law No. 2-2024, a six-month moratorium prohibiting review and approval of battery energy storage system applications.
